record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ···. Must the reciprocal-gap sum ∑_{i=1}^n λ₁/(λ_{i+1}−λ₁) be at least the corresponding value for the n-ball, namely n / (j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1} − 1) where p = (n−2)/2? In dimension 2 this is the inequality λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁) ≥ ((λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁))_disk) ≈ 1.2998.

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² show that λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁) ≥ ((λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁))|disk) ≈ 1.2998 and, more generally, for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ show that ∑_{i=1}^n λ₁/(λ_{i+1}−λ₁) ≥ n/(j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}−1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0 < \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \leq \lambda_3 \leq \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nontrivial $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$.

For real $\nu \geq 0$, let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p = (n-2)/2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_{i+1} - \lambda_1} \;\geq\; \frac{n}{\,j_{p+1,1}^{2}/j_{p,1}^{2} - 1\,},$$
the right-hand side being the corresponding quantity when $\Omega$ is an $n$-dimensional ball. Equivalently, in dimension $n=2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1} + \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_3 - \lambda_1} \;\geq\; \left( \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1} + \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_3 - \lambda_1} \right)_{\text{disk}} \approx 1.2998.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a strengthening of the Payne–Pólya–Weinberger / Ashbaugh–Benguria type isoperimetric inequalities involving sums of reciprocal gaps of low Dirichlet eigenvalues. Searches turned up related Ashbaugh–Benguria conjectures and recent work on PPW-type bounds, but no published proof of this particular reciprocal-gap-sum inequality bounded below by the ball value; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Ashbaugh–Benguria conjectures on lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues; the reciprocal-gap-sum inequality is treated as an open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the reciprocal-gap conjecture for sums involving the first n+1 Dirichlet eigenvalues remains an open Ashbaugh–Benguria type conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The Fundamental Gap (Ashbaugh, AIM)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on low eigenvalues of the Laplacian, including reciprocal gap conjectures conjectured to be extremized on balls.
status_evidence.claim: Lists the conjecture about sums of λ₁/(λ_{i+1}-λ₁) being minimized by the ball as an open problem.
